items.quote: then we will take them alive and get into the city.
items.contrast: Entering the city is expected after the capture; leaving the camp happened earlier as part of the supposed ambush.
items.reason: The king says the Arameans expect first to take the people alive and then get into the city, so the key matches the stated sequence.

items.quote: The five men who had spied out the land went inside and took the idol, the ephod and the household gods
items.contrast: The five spies enter and take the objects, while the priest and the six hundred armed men remain at the gate.
items.reason: The passage explicitly distinguishes the men performing the action from those standing at the entrance.

items.quote: “You will see it with your own eyes,” answered Elisha, “but you will not eat any of it!”
items.contrast: Elisha’s reply to the officer is that he will witness the promised event but not benefit from it; the low prices are the earlier prediction that prompted the doubt.
items.reason: The question targets Elisha’s direct response after the officer questions whether the prediction could happen.

items.quote: So we cooked my son and ate him.
items.contrast: The first child eaten is the speaking woman’s son; the other woman’s son is requested the next day but has been hidden.
items.reason: The possessive “my” identifies the first child, while the following sentence distinguishes him from the other woman’s son.

items.quote: When Athaliah heard the noise made by the guards and the people, she went to the people at the temple of the Lord.
items.contrast: Hearing the noise prompts Athaliah to go to the people; seeing the king occurs only after she arrives.
items.reason: The passage directly presents the noise as the reason for her movement and the sight of the king as a subsequent event.
